tier_reason: The README gives only a first-party headline 'up to 2x faster than revm' with no table, workloads, hardware or revm version. Public comparison code exists (crates/cli/benches/evm.rs runs revm side by side when EVM2_BENCH_REVM is set), but no results from it are published, so C.

corrections.workload: EVM bytecode execution; the README does not say which workloads back the 'up to 2x' claim. The public Criterion harness crates/cli/benches/evm.rs runs 21 transaction fixtures (fibonacci-calldata, factorial, counter, snailtracer, weth, hash_10k, erc20_transfer, push0_proxy, usdc_proxy, fiat_token, uniswap_v2_pair, univ2_router, seaport, airdrop, bswap64, bswap64_opt, eip4788, eip2935, burntpix, curve_stableswap, onchain_lm_v2) plus a mainnet block-range replay (blocks 25347446-25347455), and adds revm runs of the same cases when EVM2_BENCH_REVM=1 is set.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: CI builds with cargo codspeed build --profile profiling (inherits release: opt-level 3, panic=abort, plus full debug info) and runs CodSpeed in simulation mode; the cargo bench profile adds lto=thin and codegen-units=1. Flags and toolchain behind the README claim are not stated.
corrections.caveats: Only the headline 'up to 2x' is given; no table, workload list, hardware or revm version backs it in the README. The CI CodSpeed workflow (.github/workflows/bench.yml) does not set EVM2_BENCH_REVM, so its dashboard tracks evm2 alone, not the revm comparison; codspeed.io is also blocked from this environment. 'Up to' means best case. The comparison can be reproduced locally with EVM2_BENCH_REVM=1 cargo bench -p evm2-cli --bench evm, but no published output exists.

notes: Claim text matches the README verbatim; repo is original (not a fork), Apache-2.0 OR MIT, 72 stars, last commit 2026-10-05. Main shortcoming: unsubstantiated 'up to 2x' headline with no published numbers, though a public revm-vs-evm2 Criterion harness exists that an enricher could cite.

tier_reason: The README table (evm-bench cases timed with hyperfine) lists Guillotine, REVM, Geth and evmone with exactly the numbers in the record, but gives no CPU, compiler flags or versions, and the harness lives only in old commits and the separate first-party evmts/evm-benchmarks repo. First-party with partial methodology, so C.

corrections.caveats: First-party table with no CPU, compiler flags or versions; the harness was moved to the first-party evmts/evm-benchmarks repo. That repo's README example output shows REVM fastest on factorial (Guillotine 1.44x slower), while its generated results.md (1 internal run per benchmark, no hardware stated) shows native Guillotine faster than REVM on all 33 rows by 1.03x to 1.8x (derived from page data); most rows there are about 1-2 ms, so process startup likely dominates, and its ten-thousand-hashes time (7.46 ms) does not match the README table (2.46 ms). The README says it is on par with evmone, not faster (slower on 3 of 5 rows). Early alpha marked DO NOT USE IN PRODUCTION: 1165 of 2251 Ethereum spec tests pass (about 52%, most failures in ecmul/BN254), and the repo is 'in flux' being refactored, so the speed may omit work a conforming EVM must do. Build documented for macOS only.

notes: Numbers and derived ratios check out (1.05x to 1.48x vs REVM, 2.3x to 3.8x vs Geth). Repo MIT, 170 stars, not a fork, last commit 2026-01-04 (active). Main shortcomings: alpha with ~48% of spec tests failing, no hardware or flags, inconsistent numbers between README and the evm-benchmarks results.md.

tier_reason: The gist holds first-party raw `time` output for Life JIT, Life interpreter, wagon and wasmi on three programs, with matching return values; the workload code is public (bench/cases: Rust programs built with cargo build --release for wasm32, run via run_item.sh), but no CPU, Go version or engine versions are stated, so C.

corrections.workload: Three Rust programs in bench/cases compiled to wasm32-unknown-unknown with cargo build --release: 128-bit Pollard rho factoring, Snappy compression and recursive Fibonacci, timed end to end with the shell `time` command (bench/cases/run_item.sh), so real time includes process startup and module compilation.
corrections.caveats: Numbers date from August 2018 (gist created 2018-08-01) against the then-current wasmi (a much slower pre-register-machine design) and wagon, so they do not carry to wasmi 0.30+/1.x, wasm3 or Wasmtime. No hardware, Go version or engine versions are stated; the README only shows a chart image and links the gist. On recursive Fibonacci the Life JIT/AOT (3.898 s) is slower than Life's own interpreter (3.071 s). The repo was last committed in December 2019 and is unmaintained (not archived).

notes: Gist numbers match the record exactly and the derived ratios hold (JIT 1.5x to 6.5x vs wasmi, interpreter 1.9x to 2.4x, JIT 1.6x to 5.1x vs wagon). Only fix: the measurements are from 2018, not 2019. Repo MIT, 1.7k stars, last commit 2019-12-03, abandoned.
